text:
People Ops: Thanks everyone for joining the all-hands! If you have follow-up questions about reviews, leveling, promotions, comp, or benefits — drop them here and we'll answer live. :wave:

Alex W: Quick Q — when do managers need to submit calibration notes? I missed that slide.

People Ops: Calibration window closes next Friday at 5pm PT. If you need an extension, submit the extension form (https://intranet.redwood.example/comp-forms) and tag @People Ops.

Priya S: Is there an option for retroactive promotion if someone clearly met the bar but got missed last cycle? Manager said maybe but want the official route.

People Ops: Retroactive promotions are reserved for extenuating cases. Process: manager writes a 1-paragraph justification + evidence, attach peer feedback, then we escalate to the comp committee. Expect ~2 week turnaround. Please cc your People Ops partner.

Jordan M: Are the IC leveling rubrics getting updated? L3 -> L4 expectations felt vague in the Q&A.

Maya (CTO): Yes — we're rolling rubric v2 that clarifies scope, ownership, and design impact for each IC lane. Target publish: next Tuesday in the handbook. Alex W — I'll DM you an early draft for feedback.

Riley C: How do market adjustments work mid-year? Can someone get a merit increase outside the normal cycle for market movement?

Luis (CFO): We review market adjustments quarterly. Midyear increases for market reasons are possible but reserved for critical retention cases. Start with your manager and comp partner; they'll need benchmark data.

Alex W: Follow-up on promos + pay: if promo is effective in June, is comp bumped retroactively or only in the next cycle?

People Ops: Promotion effective date is the official point-in-time. Comp adjustments may be applied pro-rata between cycles; full band movement often aligns to the next comp cycle. We'll handle exceptions case-by-case.

Priya S: PTO — the slide mentioned "flex". Any clarity on carryover and use-it-or-lose-it?

People Ops: Carryover policy: up to 10 days carryover per year. Unused PTO beyond that after 18 months is forfeited unless manager approves an exception. Parental leave remains: 16 weeks primary, 8 weeks secondary, plus 2 weeks flexible top-up. Handbook link: https://intranet.redwood.example/benefits

Jordan M: If I disagree with my manager's review, what's the appeals process?

People Ops: Appeals window is 14 days after the manager communicates the outcome. Submit an appeal to People Ops with a short rationale and any supporting docs; we'll triage. Compensation appeals go to the comp committee for review.

Riley C: Will calibrations be name-blind? Concern about bias when managers call out names early in the process.

Maya (CTO): Good point — rubric v2 includes a name-blind first-pass for calibration. Managers submit anonymized evidence for the initial ranking; names surface later only when discussing edge cases.

People Ops: We'll compile these Qs + answers into a short FAQ and push it tomorrow. If you want a private follow-up, book People Ops office hours: https://calendar.redwood.example/peopleops-officehours or use /peopleops-help in Slack.

Alex W: Awesome — thanks. Also, is there a simple template for manager promo notes?

PeopleOps Bot: Template: 1) Promotion request summary (1-2 lines), 2) Key impact/examples (bulleted), 3) Manager recommendation + proposed effective date, 4) Relevant peer feedback links. Copy: https://intranet.redwood.example/promo-template

Priya S: TY. Will do. :heart:

People Ops: Closing note — if you raised a topic in the all-hands that didn't get covered, paste it here and we'll queue it for the FAQ or route to the right partner. :eyes:
